multilingual Wiktextract export. No individual article revision is provided.
Original headwords and per-record source hashes remain in repository evidence.

LREC 2022, pp. 1317–1325,
https://www.lrec-conf.org/proceedings/lrec2022/pdf/2022.lrec-1.140.pdf

Modifications: retain attested 3–11-letter Ukrainian headwords in lexical POS
(excluding proper names), English glosses, usage labels and form/alternative
relationships with historical wordfreq spelling Zipf >=2.5. Omit media, examples,
quotations, etymology, translations, categories and other enrichment. Tiles use
NFC and uppercase. Й/И, Ї/І, Є/Е and Ґ/Г remain distinct; Ь is one tile.
No diacritic stripping, transliteration, Latin lookalikes, stress marks, hyphens
or spaces are accepted. Apostrophized words are excluded, never silently
respelt by deleting required apostrophes. Canonical source spelling is retained.
Up to eight source entries and eight senses per entry accompany each guess.
Broad guesses include attested inflections, alternatives and labelled uncommon,
historical, regional or sensitive senses. Answers require a standalone eligible
sense, Zipf >=4.3 and explicit independent model editorial approval, except
individually reviewed ҐРУНТ (soil/ground), exact spelling Zipf 3.82. This one
ordinary lemma is an explicit editorial exception; its historical sense does
not qualify it, and Ґ/Г are never merged.
Selection targets contemporary standard Ukrainian in Ukraine, not exhaustive
regional separation. No native-human review or certification is claimed.

Frequency: wordfreq 3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, revision
372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b, small_uk.msgpack.gz.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b
SHA-256: c8cc895dd13da4a905d268d96382f2675f49fed770e89804c4f8f114a2564dec
Data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Software: MIT. Complete pinned README and MIT notice supplied.
Preserve all README source credits including OpenSubtitles and freely available
SUBTLEX, Marc Brysbaert and coauthors. No corpus sentences are redistributed.
For case-normalized spellings retain the maximum estimate, not a sum. No letter
aliases are applied to frequency. Historical spelling frequency does not prove
current Ukraine-specific commonness or sense frequency.

Sources, pins, policy and reproduction: docs/ukrainian-sources.md and
src/data/ukrainian/source.json in https://github.com/intrepion/kata-inspired-by-wordle-codex-dot
No VESUM data is used. Preserve attribution, modification notices and ShareAlike
terms when redistributing adapted data. These notices add no extra restrictions.
